newsitem.title: USA: Japan, US agree excessive forex moves undesirable.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US agree excessive forex moves undesirable.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin have agreed that excessive currency moves are undesirable, a senior Japanese government official told reporters on Saturday.
"The message of the April G7 agreement on exchange rates has firmly penetrated into currency markets," said the official who asked for anonymity.

The statement by finance ministers of the Group of Seven industrial nations in April stipulated that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility and significant deviations from fundamentals are undesirable.
Referring to a Mitsuzuka-Rubin meeting on Friday, the official said Rubin did not ask for additional Japanese fiscal spending to stimulate the economy.
They agreed that Japan and the U.S. will continue to closely cooperate in dealing with excessive currency moves, the official said.
A G7 statement issued on Saturday by the G7 heads of state said Japan has the objective of achieving strong domestic demand-led growth.
The official said G7 finance ministers, who had a separate meeting on Saturday, did not spend much time discussing exchange rates.
